title: From Code That Produces Results to Code That Makes Them Trustworthy
text:
After the Scenario–Sweep–Run–Dashboard workflow was in place, a more difficult question remained: does the existence of a curve make it scientifically interpretable?
PySDM-Seeding-Lab PR #3, merged on 14 July 2026, focused on provenance, numerical quality, durable failure evidence, and reproducibility. Its 12 commits and 78 changed files moved the project from a functional app toward a qualified research platform.

title: From Code That Produces Results to Code That Makes Them Trustworthy
text:
Every diagnostic needs a provenance
Early Growth Pathway views sometimes used proxy values when the adapter did not expose a native product. In a dashboard, a proxy column looked too similar to a direct model output. Every diagnostic is now classified as:



Class
Meaning




native
Directly from a PySDM product or state


derived
Calculated explicitly from native values


proxy
Approximation used for workflow validation


missing
Not provided by the current adapter



Each result includes diagnostic_provenance.json, and the dashboard shows counts and warnings. The verified native parcel contract currently reports 11 native, 2 derived, and 0 proxy diagnostics. More importantly, future variables cannot enter the scientific view without declaring their origin.
Native or radius-filtered outputs now cover thermodynamics, water-vapour mixing ratio, cloud and rain water, droplet concentrations, effective radii, and all-activated water and number. Cloud and rain remain instantaneous wet-radius bins, not particle-history classifications—an interpretation constraint recorded with the result.

title: From Code That Produces Results to Code That Makes Them Trustworthy
section: From mean radius to spectrum transition
text:
From mean radius to spectrum transition
An effective mean radius cannot show whether only part of the population moved into rain-size bins. The lab now writes wet-radius spectra at configurable checkpoints, with bin boundaries, number concentration, liquid-volume fraction, and unactivated/cloud/rain regimes.
Rain boundaries are audited at 20, 25, and 30 \(\mu\mathrm{m}\). Spectrum transition—the first time rain-size liquid exceeds a fraction of activated liquid—is tested at 0.5%, 1%, and 2%. The 1% value is explicitly a project-owned operational threshold, not a universal observational standard.
Reporting threshold sensitivity prevents one convenient cutoff from masquerading as a physical law.

title: From Code That Produces Results to Code That Makes Them Trustworthy
text:
Source-aware water budget
Hygroscopic injection deliberately adds a source. Treating the injection window as a closed system would misclassify the intended source as numerical drift. Water-budget output therefore separates vapour, cloud water, rain water, total water, and the source interval. Closed-budget checks are evaluated before and after injection, while the source window remains explicitly recorded.

title: From Code That Produces Results to Code That Makes Them Trustworthy
text:
Qualification with real PySDM runs
Numerical convergence varies timestep and background and seeding super-droplet resolution while holding the other axes fixed.
timestep: 5 / 10 / 15 s
seeding super-droplets: 100 / 200 / 400
background super-droplets: 100 / 200 / 400
The standard qualification completed 27 parameter cases and 54 real PySDM executions with zero failures. For non-zero next-finest comparisons, 12 of 12 checks were within 5%; the median relative difference was 0.187%, P95 was 1.140%, and the maximum was 1.731%.
This evidence supports the 5% default only for the tested marine, condensation/seeding, collision-OFF profile. Rain metrics were zero, so it does not establish convergence for collision-ON, rain-producing experiments. A passing number without its scope would be misleading.

title: From Code That Produces Results to Code That Makes Them Trustworthy
text:
Failure evidence: 281-character paths
A nested experiment requested 24 sweep cases and 10 ensemble members per case—240 members in total. Every member failed because repeated parameter labels pushed Windows output paths to roughly 281 characters.
The solution was to separate human-readable scientific metadata from filesystem identity:
cases/case_001/
members/member_001/
comparison/
single/
Labels and values remain in configuration and metadata. Execution health is now success, partial, or failed, and member/case exceptions are saved before a total failure is propagated. The dashboard can distinguish “no physical response” from “no valid execution.”

title: From Code That Produces Results to Code That Makes Them Trustworthy
text:
The 24-member memory benchmark
The large benchmark completed 24 of 24 requested members in 743.878 seconds. RSS grew from 111.34 MiB to a 1,110.98 MiB peak and remained at 1,064.70 MiB after completion.
By contrast, streaming aggregation of the 24 CSV files took 3.772 seconds and added only 0.270 MiB of RSS. This shows that the aggregator is memory-bounded and points future profiling toward retained PySDM, backend, or JIT state. The evidence does not yet identify one component as a memory leak.

title: From Code That Produces Results to Code That Makes Them Trustworthy
section: A result directory as a research record
text:
A result directory as a research record
New results can include report.md, self-contained report.html, report.pdf, and result_manifest.json. Reports collect configuration, adapter, provenance, validation, main metrics, water-budget and convergence status, spectrum transition, artifacts, reproduction commands, and interpretation constraints.
The versioned manifest records schema and reader compatibility. Legacy results without manifests and schema-v1 aliases are preserved as migration fixtures so that new readers do not silently abandon old experiments.
Validation included 23 unit/integration tests, two of them using real PySDM, plus project-integrity and key Streamlit application tests.
The remaining work is equally important: collision-ON rain-producing qualification, ownership profiling for retained RSS, observational review of the 1% transition threshold, and numerical equality tests for a future columnar cache.
PR #2 made experiments runnable and traceable. PR #3 attached provenance, quality, failure state, and scope to every result. The quality of research software is not the number of figures it can draw, but how explicitly it records where it may be wrong.

title: From Simulation Code to a Research Workflow: PySDM Seeding Lab v1.0.0
text:
Release update (21 July 2026). PR #5 was merged into main, and merge commit d0fc97e was published as PySDM Seeding Lab v1.0.0. The main release CI passed Windows and Ubuntu fast regression plus real PySDM integration on Ubuntu.
The previous development log separated absolute rain-state qualification from seeding-response qualification, then connected common seeds, process isolation, detached jobs, and bounded parallel execution. Experiments could finally survive a long night on the lab server. What remained open was a project-level contract: How much computation is enough, how should model transitions be compared with observations, and what can v1.0 actually claim?
PySDM-Seeding-Lab PR #5, at its 21 July 2026 checkpoint, answers those questions across 16 commits and 71 changed files, with 7,054 additions and 98 deletions. This was not a changelog-sized feature bundle. It was an effort to place execution planning, numerical qualification, observation-mapping review, reporting, and scientific limitations in one evidence chain.

title: From Simulation Code to a Research Workflow: PySDM Seeding Lab v1.0.0
section: Turning an open-ended project into one bounded question
text:
Turning an open-ended project into one bounded question
PR #4 left six practical and scientific problems unresolved:

Would the seeding-minus-control response converge at a finer reference resolution?
Could an interrupted qualification safely resume without rerunning valid members?
Could the Streamlit dashboard avoid repeatedly parsing large CSV files?
What contract would align a model spectrum transition with an observed drizzle event?
How should real observations be retained when they do not map cleanly to parcel time?
Where should an expanding development program stop and call itself v1.0?

These are all reproducibility questions. Reproducing a result requires more than a successful number: the reason for running a calculation, the rejected interpretation, and the unusable evidence must survive beside it. The sixteen commits in PR #5 therefore move from a finer targeted run to a machine-checked scientific claim boundary.

title: From Simulation Code to a Research Workflow: PySDM Seeding Lab v1.0.0
section: Asking the high-resolution question in 40 runs, not 70
text:
Asking the high-resolution question in 40 runs, not 70
The original rain_response_standard plan called for a 2.5 s timestep, 1,600 seeded and 1,600 background super-droplets, and five common random seeds. Running its complete plan would require 70 control/seeding executions. Pilot evidence had already shown that absolute state and response behaved very differently, so executing every combination was not automatically the best scientific question.
The new targeted qualification plan retains only the finest reference and each numerical axis’s next-finest comparison:
4 one-factor-at-reference cases
× 5 common random seeds
× control / seeding
= 40 physical PySDM executions
That is 42.9% less work than the 70-execution plan without removing a comparison used by the 5% convergence decision. A dry run freezes the plan first; the confirmed qualification then runs serially with one worker so its resource commitment remains explicit.
Long runs can still be interrupted. Resume does not trust a directory merely because its name exists. A member is reusable only when its normalized execution configuration has the same SHA-256 fingerprint and its configuration, summary, and CSV are readable and successful. Missing, corrupt, failed, and configuration-mismatched members are rerun. Aggregation, evidence, and reports are rebuilt, while each attempt records reuse and rerun counts in qualification_plan.json.

title: From Simulation Code to a Research Workflow: PySDM Seeding Lab v1.0.0
section: Doubling repeated-read speed without replacing CSV
text:
Doubling repeated-read speed without replacing CSV
Repeated dashboard views made large CSV parsing increasingly expensive. Replacing CSV with a binary format would also replace the human-readable provenance, migration, and download contract.
The columnar-cache design keeps CSV as the canonical source of truth and stores Arrow IPC in a hidden, disposable cache. A missing, corrupt, or stale cache is rebuilt from CSV. Systems without pyarrow, and tables below the default size threshold, continue to read CSV. Arrow is a rebuildable performance layer, not a scientific result.
The benchmark repeatedly read a real 101 × 505 result with 51,005 cells:



Format
Raw CSV
Cold build/read
Warm cache
Warm / CSV




Parquet prototype
24.981 ms
370.801 ms
33.058 ms
0.756×


Arrow IPC v2
16.271 ms
61.597 ms
8.076 ms
2.015×



Warm Arrow reduced latency by about 50.4%, reached break-even after roughly seven total reads, and occupied 1.2467 times the CSV storage. Parquet was not selected merely because it is familiar: it was slower than CSV for this result shape. Exact dataframe equality and measured behavior—not format preference—made the decision.
The Parquet screening and Arrow IPC confirmation were separate sequential runs, so the meaningful comparison is each format’s ratio to its own CSV baseline rather than a direct comparison of absolute timings.

title: From Simulation Code to a Research Workflow: PySDM Seeding Lab v1.0.0
section: Separating observation ingestion from observational validation
text:
Separating observation ingestion from observational validation
Before comparing the model’s internal 1% rain-liquid transition with observed drizzle onset, the project needed to define what one observation event means. The new observation-event contract requires event and case identity, onset and uncertainty, model-time offset, time origin, source ID, observation method, event definition, sampling context, and mapping status.
An immutable comparison package records every threshold candidate, onset error, RMSE, within-uncertainty fraction, source hashes, and a manifest. The lowest-MAE candidate is never promoted automatically to a calibration. Synthetic rows test only software behavior; even real observations remain spatiotemporal_proxy when sampled volume and parcel time are not defensibly aligned.

BASTALIAS: real data from a moving volume
The EUREC4A BASTALIAS importer extracts persistent drizzle detections from approximately 1.5 s airborne radar–lidar NetCDF data. It retains the source file’s full SHA-256 and sensitivity across the -15, -17, and -20 dBZ cloud–drizzle boundaries. All 400 samples in the reviewed ten-minute window passed the time quality flag; the selected -20 dBZ event appeared 7.121 s after the window began.
The aircraft, however, observes different horizontal volumes as it moves. A persistent echo is not necessarily the temporal history of one parcel. The importer therefore forces mapping_status = spatiotemporal_proxy even though the evidence class is observation. The pipeline compared the event against 27 model candidates, but produced zero direct-temporal rows. The mapping audit explicitly prevents those rankings from calibrating the operational 1% floor.


ARM ENA: a fixed column is still not a parcel history
The ARM ENA pipeline selects fixed-column KAZR/KAZRARSCL data as the next candidate. Credentials are accepted only through environment variables; partial downloads are atomically replaced; source hashes, QC fields, height selection, and -20/-17/-15 dBZ sensitivity are retained in the package.
A zenith radar is closer to a time series than a moving aircraft, but it observes an Eulerian column through which wind advects different parcels. Radar reflectivity is also not the model’s rain-liquid fraction. No ARM credential or real source file was available at this checkpoint, so a synthetic ARM-format NetCDF verified software behavior only. The candidate audit therefore closes the v1.0 investigation with a proxy disposition, not a successful external calibration.

title: From Simulation Code to a Research Workflow: PySDM Seeding Lab v1.0.0
section: The finer run found a boundary, not an effect
text:
The finer run found a boundary, not an effect
The targeted-run evidence completed all 20 case-seed pairs and all 40 physical executions, with zero failed cases and zero failed members.









Qualification family
Within 5%
Maximum error
v1.0 decision




Absolute control/seeding rain state
60 / 60
4.180%
Supported for the tested profile


Seeding-minus-control response
11 / 105
2465.158%
Quantitative response unsupported



All five finest-reference seeds had a positive final rain-response direction, with a mean final difference of about 0.0001377 kg/kg. That 5/5 result is neither a confidence interval nor a significance test, and it is not a converged effect estimate. Every seed independently rejected response support. Maximum response errors along the timestep, seeded super-droplet count, and background super-droplet count axes were 1630.411%, 2272.468%, and 2465.158%, respectively.
The turning point was refusing to rename a desirable sign as an effect. Absolute rain state is supported only for the reviewed collision-ON marine profile, its four OFAT cases, five common seeds, and finest-to-next-finest comparisons. The smaller difference between two states did not converge with resolution. Rather than launch all 70 executions in hope of a pass, the workflow preserves direction and spread as descriptive results and convergence as a separate rejected claim.

title: From Simulation Code to a Research Workflow: PySDM Seeding Lab v1.0.0
section: Managing scientific claims with a schema
text:
Managing scientific claims with a schema
A limitation written only in a paragraph is easy for the next analysis or UI to forget. PR #5 makes release/v1_scientific_scope.json the machine-readable source of truth for claim order, status, scope, limitations, and evidence.

Tests now prevent “observation ingested” from silently becoming “model validated,” or “positive sign” from becoming “effect established.” Preserving evidence that cannot support a claim is part of reproducibility too.

title: From Simulation Code to a Research Workflow: PySDM Seeding Lab v1.0.0
section: Giving v1.0 a finite finish line

title: From Simulation Code to a Research Workflow: PySDM Seeding Lab v1.0.0
section: Not avoiding failure, but making it interpretable
text:
Not avoiding failure, but making it interpretable
Completing the v1.0.0 release candidate does not mean every scientific question produced a positive answer. It means the workflow can reproduce where the answer stops.

Absolute rain state is numerically supported within a limited tested profile.
Response direction is descriptive, while quantitative response is unsupported.
The 1% floor is an operational definition, not a universal drizzle-onset standard.
BASTALIAS and ARM ENA are valuable observation proxies, not Lagrangian parcel calibrations.
Surface rainfall gain, causal effect, and real-world cloud-seeding efficacy are outside v1.0’s claims.

The project did not fail because the desired convergence did not appear. It learned how to decide, reproducibly, what the evidence permits us to say. Simulation code becomes a research workflow when the scope of each number survives alongside the number itself.

title: From Simulation Code to a Research Workflow: PySDM Seeding Lab v1.0.0
section: Questions deliberately left for v1.1 and later research
text:
Questions deliberately left for v1.1 and later research
The following work remains outside the finite v1.0 gate:

measuring real-PySDM server scaling for serial, four-worker, and eight-worker execution;
direct Lagrangian observation mapping with parcel trajectories and residence times;
additional datasets for transition-threshold and cadence review; and
stronger convergence and matched-observation evidence before any quantitative seeding-response claim.

v1.0.0 does not pretend to have answered these questions. It leaves an executable contract for what the next experiment must establish—and what language remains off limits until it does.

title: Experiment 2. Sensitivity to Seeded-Particle Properties and Injection Timing
text:
NoteProvenance



Neither the main experiment nor the follow-up used PySDM-Seeding-Lab. Both were independent PySDM parcel studies developed in Visual Studio Code and run on the laboratory server. This page combines the 2 July sensitivity study and the 3 July diagnostic follow-up.

title: Experiment 2. Sensitivity to Seeded-Particle Properties and Injection Timing
section: Which particle should be injected, and when?
text:
Which particle should be injected, and when?
Experiment 1 showed that rain-water response is sensitive to representation and random seed. Here, n_sd_initial = n_sd_seeding = 1,000 was fixed while three physical controls were varied: seeded-particle dry radius, hygroscopicity κ, and injection window.
The PySDM seeding_no_collisions parcel framework was extended to four cases per condition: no seeding and seeding with collision ON, then the same pair with collision OFF. Every reported effect is seeding minus its matching no-seeding baseline.








Sensitivity axis
Values
Fixed settings




Dry radius
0.5, 1.0, 2.0 µm
κ = 0.8, 15–20 min


κ
0.3, 0.5, 0.8, 1.0
dry radius = 1 µm, 15–20 min


Injection timing
10–15, 15–20, 20–25 min
dry radius = 1 µm, κ = 0.8



The main study used a 10-member ensemble with Formulae seeds 100–109. Rain water was the water mixing ratio carried by particles with wet radius at least 25 µm.

title: Experiment 2. Sensitivity to Seeded-Particle Properties and Injection Timing
text:
Dry radius



Rain-water response for dry radii of 0.5, 1, and 2 µm.


With collision ON, the final response followed 2 µm > 1 µm > 0.5 µm. Approximate values on the plotted scale were \(2.1\times10^{-5}\), \(0.9\times10^{-5}\), and \(0.4\)–\(0.5\times10^{-5}\).
Larger dry particles can reach larger wet sizes and participate in coalescence more readily. However, this was a fixed-number design: increasing dry radius also increased total injected dry mass. The result cannot be interpreted as a pure size effect. That confounding factor motivates the fixed-mass design in Experiment 3.

title: Experiment 2. Sensitivity to Seeded-Particle Properties and Injection Timing
text:
Hygroscopicity κ



Rain-water sensitivity to κ from 0.3 to 1.0.


The late response ranked κ = 1.0 > 0.8 > 0.5 > 0.3, with approximate final values of \(1.0\), \(0.9\), \(0.75\), and \(0.65\times10^{-5}\). More hygroscopic particles took up water more readily and entered the collision pathway more effectively.
Collision-OFF rain water remained nearly zero across κ. That does not mean nothing changed: vapour, number, and cloud-size radius diagnostics may respond even when condensation alone does not cross the 25 µm threshold.

title: Experiment 2. Sensitivity to Seeded-Particle Properties and Injection Timing
text:
Injection timing



Rain-water response for 10–15, 15–20, and 20–25 min injection windows.


Injection at 10–15 min produced a brief positive spike followed by a negative excursion to roughly \(-3.8\times10^{-5}\) and ended near zero. Early injection may have increased vapour competition and small-droplet number before efficient rain-size growth was possible.
The 15–20 min window produced a smoother positive response ending near \(0.9\times10^{-5}\). The 20–25 min window rose rapidly after 22–23 min and ended near \(2.7\times10^{-5}\), the largest of the three. Because this window is close to the end of the simulation, a large late value does not establish long-term persistence; a longer integration is required.

title: Experiment 2. Sensitivity to Seeded-Particle Properties and Injection Timing
text:
Follow-up: tracing the growth pathway
The first analysis emphasized rain water but could not explain the intermediate mechanism. Some concentration and effective-radius products had insufficient finite data or natural NaN intervals.
The follow-up separated particles into cloud-size (0.5–25 µm), rain-size (≥25 µm), and all activated (≥0.5 µm) ranges. It expanded ensemble output from the mean to standard deviation, median, q25, q75, successful-member count, and finite fraction. A rain effective radius is naturally undefined before rain-size particles exist, so NaN intervals were evaluated with product-health checks rather than treated automatically as failed runs.
The diagnostics support the following pathway:
seeded-particle injection
→ vapour consumption
→ RH / supersaturation depletion
→ condensational growth and latent heating
→ cloud-size water redistribution
→ collision/coalescence (collision ON)
→ rain-size mass increase
Collision OFF could still alter vapour and cloud-size particles, but it produced almost no rain-water increase. With collision ON, vapour and RH/supersaturation decreased, temperature and all-activated water increased, and rain-water mass rose. Number and mass must be read together: coalescence may reduce particle count while increasing individual mass and effective radius.

Conclusion. Within the tested range, larger dry radius, higher κ, and 20–25 min injection produced stronger late rain-water responses. Dry radius remained confounded with injected mass, and late timing remained confounded with the simulation endpoint, so these are hypotheses for the next experiment—not universal optima.

The next step introduces multiple background aerosol environments and separates fixed-number from fixed-mass injection in Experiment 3.

title: Experiment 4. A κ–Radius–Timing Response Surface
text:
NoteProvenance



This experiment was not executed in PySDM-Seeding-Lab. It used separate PySDM scripts in Visual Studio Code on the laboratory server. Every “maximum” below is limited to the tested parameter range and is not an operational optimum.

title: Experiment 4. A κ–Radius–Timing Response Surface
section: Can seeding response be compressed into an empirical law?
text:
Can seeding response be compressed into an empirical law?
Previous experiments varied dry radius, κ, and injection timing one axis at a time. Yet κ and radius are coupled through activation, while injection timing changes both available growth time and cloud maturity.
Experiment 4 asks whether dry radius or κ dominates, whether they can be combined as \(kappa r_{dry}^3\), whether timing interacts with activation strength, and whether final rain-water response can be represented by an empirical surface.

title: Experiment 4. A κ–Radius–Timing Response Surface
text:
From preliminary tests to Experiment 4-3
Experiment 4-1 established an initial surface. Experiment 4-2 extended radius to 10 µm, but direct crossing of the 25 µm rain threshold by very large seeds began to dominate interpretation. These were diagnostic steps, not failures.
Experiment 4-3 narrowed the interpretable radius range to 0.5–6.0 µm and sampled it at 0.1 µm spacing. It became the main dataset.
collision = ON
terminal velocity = RogersYau
κ = 0.3–2.0, step 0.1       → 18 values
dry radius = 0.5–6.0 µm     → 56 values
injection = 15–20 / 20–25 min
ensemble seeds = 20
t_max = 30 min
The grid contains \(18\times56\times2=2{,}016\) conditions. Each used 20 ensemble seeds and the same no-seeding baseline. The main objective was final rain-water difference \(J_{final}\); integrated positive and maximum responses were secondary metrics.

title: Experiment 4. A κ–Radius–Timing Response Surface
section: Monotonic response toward larger κ and radius
text:
Monotonic response toward larger κ and radius



Final response surfaces for the two injection windows.


Both windows increased toward larger κ and dry radius. Radius showed the stronger, nearly monotonic effect; κ was weaker but consistently positive. Only one decreasing case occurred among 1,904 adjacent κ comparisons.
The 20–25 min window exceeded the 15–20 min window across every tested condition. The late/early \(J_{final}\) ratio averaged about 1.36 and ranged from 1.29 to 1.46.
The maximum occurred at the upper boundary: κ = 2.0, dry radius = 6.0 µm, and 20–25 min. Because it lies on a boundary, it is only the maximum inside this grid—not a universal optimum.

title: Experiment 4. A κ–Radius–Timing Response Surface
text:
Activation strength and timing
Define a Köhler-like activation coordinate:
\[
A=\log\!\left(\kappa r_{dry}^{3}\right).
\]
The final response was fitted with a quadratic function of activation coordinate \(A\) and injection coordinate \(\tau\):
\[
J_{final}=\beta_0+\beta_1A+\beta_2\tau+\beta_3A^2+\beta_4\tau^2+\beta_5A\tau+\epsilon.
\]



Activation-strength collapse for the two injection windows.


The two injection windows formed separated curves. Timing is therefore not merely a constant offset; it interacts with particle strength. The positive interaction coefficient indicates that strong particles and later injection reinforced one another within this model configuration.



Term
Coefficient




\(\beta_0\) intercept
\(1.59\times10^{-6}\)


\(\beta_1\) activation linear
\(-3.16\times10^{-5}\)


\(\beta_2\) timing linear
\(2.90\times10^{-5}\)


\(\beta_3\) activation curvature
\(6.73\times10^{-6}\)


\(\beta_4\) timing curvature
\(3.80\times10^{-5}\)


\(\beta_5\) activation × timing
\(4.69\times10^{-5}\)






Fitted empirical relationship and reported coefficients.


The fit achieved \(R^2=0.970\), RMSE \(=1.23\times10^{-5}\), and \(n=2{,}016\). This is an empirical compression of one fixed background, collision model, threshold, timing definition, and parameter normalization. It is not a universal physical law.
Radius enters activation strength through a cubic volume term and dominated κ over this range. Higher κ consistently supported activation and water uptake. Later injection allowed seeded particles to interact with a more mature parcel state.

Conclusion. Within the tested range, \(J_{final}\) was well organized by \(\log(\kappa r_{dry}^3)\) and injection timing. Dry radius supplied the dominant main effect, while late injection reinforced strong particles. The upper-boundary maximum is a direction for the next grid, not a final optimum.

title: Experiment 4. A κ–Radius–Timing Response Surface
text:
Next research
A generalized response law should add fixed-number versus fixed-mass dose normalization, background aerosol sensitivity, a cloud-maturity/updraft coordinate instead of absolute time, and joint dependence on particle property, dose, background, and cloud state.

title: Experiment 6. Does the Seeding Conclusion Depend on the Terminal-Velocity Formula?
text:
NoteProvenance



This experiment was also performed outside PySDM-Seeding-Lab. Separate scripts that reuse the Experiment 5 parcel code with only the terminal-velocity formula swapped were run on the laboratory server. These are not Seeding Lab results.

title: Experiment 6. Does the Seeding Conclusion Depend on the Terminal-Velocity Formula?
section: Question: where does 6 mm come from, and does the conclusion lean on the formula?
text:
Question: where does 6 mm come from, and does the conclusion lean on the formula?
Every metric in Experiment 5 was the maximum rain water “before the largest drop exceeds 6 mm”. This experiment asks two things.

Is 6 mm a physical limit or a code limit?
If the terminal-velocity formula changes, does the sign pattern of Experiment 5 (updraft × injection timing) survive, and how much does the effect size change?

The goal is not to pick “the most accurate formula” but to see how robust the existing conclusion is to that choice.

title: Experiment 6. Does the Seeding Conclusion Depend on the Terminal-Velocity Formula?
section: 6 mm was an implementation limit, not physics
text:
6 mm was an implementation limit, not physics
Gunn and Kinzer measured the fall speed of more than 1,500 water droplets in stagnant air (760 mmHg, 20 °C, RH 50%) (Gunn and Kinzer 1949). The largest drop in their table has a diameter of 5.8 mm and falls at 9.17 m s⁻¹. A 5.8 mm diameter is a 2.9 mm radius.
PySDM’s GunnKinzer1949 converts this table to radius, fits an RBF interpolant, evaluates it on a lookup grid for radius 0–6 mm, and raises a ValueError when an input radius exceeds 6 mm (below 40 µm radius it overrides the table with a small-drop approximation). The 2.9–6 mm radius range is therefore extrapolation, not measurement, and 6 mm is the upper bound of the code that builds the lookup table. Earlier runs used this formula, so they stopped with an error the moment a drop passed 6 mm. Experiment 5 switched to Rogers–Yau, which has no upper bound, and interpreted only pre-6-mm values.
The real problem is not the formula, though. With no sedimentation and no breakup in the parcel, a large drop keeps growing. In the strong-updraft controls of Experiment 5 the largest drop reached about 3 cm radius. Changing the terminal-velocity formula does not supply the missing physics.






WarningRadius and diameter



PySDM and the experiments on this blog use radius; the Gunn–Kinzer table uses diameter. “6 mm” means a 6 mm radius (12 mm diameter), and “2.9 mm” a 2.9 mm radius (5.8 mm diameter).

title: Experiment 6. Does the Seeding Conclusion Depend on the Terminal-Velocity Formula?
section: But strong + late was hardly tested
text:
But strong + late was hardly tested



Cumulative distribution of the time at which strong-updraft runs reached the 2.9 mm common limit. Left: controls; right: seeded runs.


Weak-updraft runs never reached 2.9 mm with any formula and ran the full 40 min. All 380 strong-updraft runs of every formula, however, stopped at 2.9 mm between about 12 and 26 min. Late injection starts at 15 min, so the strong + late analysis window ended at a median of 15.5–16.8 min depending on the formula. With Rogers–Yau, 40% of strong + late runs stopped before injection even began, and three clean-background cases (coarse low, giant low, giant medium) gave exactly the same value, +0.0006 g kg⁻¹, despite different seed sizes and doses. The run ended before the seeds could reach the metric. The strong + late row above therefore cannot test the “strong + late enhancement” of Experiment 5. What this experiment actually checks is the two weak rows and strong + early.

title: Experiment 6. Does the Seeding Conclusion Depend on the Terminal-Velocity Formula?
text:
Result 2. Magnitudes differed by formula

The overall mean from Rogers–Yau was 1.3–1.9 times that of the other formulas. Rogers–Yau produced the largest enhancement under weak updraft and the weakest suppression for strong + early.
The most formula-sensitive condition was clean · strong · early · fine · medium. All five formulas gave suppression, but its size ranged from −0.24 (Rogers–Yau) to −0.69 g kg⁻¹ (Gunn–Kinzer), about a 2.8-fold spread.
The most robust condition was polluted · weak · early · giant · high, at +0.387 to +0.393 g kg⁻¹ for all five formulas.

The terminal-velocity formula affected the size more than the sign. This is one more reason to read the magnitudes of Experiment 5 as descriptive only.

title: Experiment 6. Does the Seeding Conclusion Depend on the Terminal-Velocity Formula?
section: What can and cannot be said
text:
What can and cannot be said







Category
Content




Supported
6 mm is the ceiling of PySDM’s lookup table (the observations end at 2.9 mm radius) · all five formulas give strong + early suppression 16/18 and weak + early enhancement 12/18 · scenario sign agreement of 95.8–100%


Descriptive
The 1.3–1.9-fold spread in mean effect and the ~2.8-fold spread in the sensitive condition — unconverged, and the mean is pulled by a few conditions


Not shown
Robustness of strong + late (mostly cut off by the common stop) · which formula best matches observations · growth beyond 2.9 mm · results with sedimentation or breakup




Conclusion. Across five terminal-velocity formulas, strong + early suppression (16/18) and weak + early enhancement (12/18) stayed the same, and scenario signs agreed with Rogers–Yau in 95.8–100% of cases. The mean effect size, however, differed by a factor of 1.3–1.9, and strong + late was effectively untested because of the 2.9 mm common stop. The terminal-velocity formula is an uncertainty axis for magnitude more than for sign.

The paper reports seed size as diameter, so units must be matched carefully against my radius-based experiments.

title: Starting with PySDM: First Coordinates for Cloud Microphysics Experiments
text: The best place to begin learning a numerical model is not “Which code should I run?” but “What am I trying to represent?” This first note outlines PySDM’s role in cloud microphysics and maps the experimental path this blog will follow.

title: Starting with PySDM: First Coordinates for Cloud Microphysics Experiments
text:
What does PySDM represent?
PySDM is an open-source package for simulating the dynamics of particle populations. Its current development focuses on the microphysics of aerosols, cloud droplets, and raindrops in moist air. It uses the Super-Droplet Method (SDM) to represent a vast number of real particles with a smaller number of computational particles (Shima et al. 2009; Bartman et al. 2022).
Consider a super-droplet described by radius \(r_i\) and multiplicity \(\xi_i\). The \(k\)-th moment of the real particle population can be approximated by a sum over computational particles:
\[
M_k \approx \sum_i \xi_i r_i^k
\]
\(k=0\) relates to number concentration, while \(k=3\) relates to volume or mass. Decisions such as how many computational particles to use and how to sample the initial distribution are therefore not mere implementation details; they are experimental conditions that directly affect statistical quality.

title: Starting with PySDM: First Coordinates for Cloud Microphysics Experiments
text:
First environment check
The latest PySDM release can be installed with pip. Unless noted otherwise, code blocks on this blog are illustrative. The actual reproducible environment will follow the pinned dependency files in PySDM-Seeding-Lab.
python -m pip install PySDM
After installation, the smallest useful check is whether the package imports in the current environment and which version was selected.
from importlib.metadata import version

import PySDM

print("PySDM import: OK")
print("PySDM version:", version("PySDM"))






Tip



Experiment notes will record the operating system, random seed, and repository commit alongside the Python and PySDM versions. It is a small habit that turns “it worked on my machine” into a research record.

title: Starting with PySDM: First Coordinates for Cloud Microphysics Experiments
text:
Three stages ahead

1. Learn PySDM
After understanding SDM state variables and moments, we will examine how environments, dynamics, and products divide responsibilities. Instead of stopping after running official examples, each object will be annotated with the physical assumption it represents.


2. Build the Lab
We will establish an isolated Python environment and clear conventions for configuration files, data, and figures. Every experiment will include a command that reruns it and a minimal validation that checks the result.


3. Experiments
We will first create a baseline, then vary conditions such as seeding time, particle-size distribution, and dosage one at a time. Interpretable metrics such as water budget, number concentration, and spectral moments will take priority over differences in a single curve.

title: Starting with PySDM: First Coordinates for Cloud Microphysics Experiments
text:
First checkpoint
Before moving to the next note, there are four things to check:

PySDM can be imported in an isolated environment.
Python and PySDM versions can be recorded together.
The meaning of a super-droplet’s multiplicity can be explained.
Fixed conditions can be distinguished between baseline and seeding experiments.

Once these checkpoints are complete, the next step will dissect one official PySDM example by following the flow of inputs, dynamics, and products. The PySDM v2 paper is a useful map of the package structure and its extended capabilities (Jong et al. 2023).

title: From One CCN to a Raindrop: Warm-Cloud Microphysics
text: At the April lab meeting I reported, as part of my progress update, the notes I had taken on the warm-cloud part (Section 3.1) of chapter 3 (Cloud Microphysics) of Houze’s Cloud Dynamics. This post rewrites those notes after checking them against the textbook. Equation numbers follow the second edition (2014) (Houze 2014). The question: how does an aerosol particle of about 0.1 µm become a cloud droplet, how does a cloud droplet become a raindrop, and where in between does hygroscopic seeding intervene?

title: From One CCN to a Raindrop: Warm-Cloud Microphysics
section: 1. Pure droplets cannot form on their own: the Kelvin effect
text:
1. Pure droplets cannot form on their own: the Kelvin effect
The net energy needed for vapour molecules to come together by chance into a pure-water embryo of radius \(R\) is
\[
\begin{aligned}
\Delta E &= 4\pi R^2\sigma_{vl} - \tfrac{4}{3}\pi R^3 n_l\,(\mu_v-\mu_l) \\
\mu_v-\mu_l &= k_B T \ln S
\end{aligned} \tag{3.1–3.2}
\]
In words: “net cost of the embryo = cost of creating new surface − gain from molecules entering the liquid.” \(\sigma_{vl}\) is the work needed to create a unit area of vapour–liquid interface (surface tension), \(n_l\) is the number of molecules per unit volume of the drop, and \(\mu_v-\mu_l\) is the Gibbs free-energy difference for one molecule moving from vapour to liquid. If \(S<1\) both terms are costs and the embryo always evaporates. If \(S>1\), the surface term (\(R^2\)) wins at small \(R\) and the volume term (\(R^3\)) at large \(R\), creating an energy barrier. Locating its top with \(\partial(\Delta E)/\partial R=0\) gives Kelvin’s formula:
\[
R_c = \frac{2\sigma_{vl}}{n_l k_B T \ln S}
\tag{3.3}
\]
Embryos smaller than \(R_c\) evaporate; only those that happen to exceed \(R_c\) keep growing. At saturation (\(S=1\)), \(\ln S=0\) and \(R_c\to\infty\), so supersaturation is essential. Computing it at 10 °C makes the point:

According to the textbook, the homogeneous nucleation rate shoots up only when \(S\) reaches about 4–5, that is, at supersaturations of 300–400%, whereas atmospheric supersaturation seldom exceeds 1%. Homogeneous nucleation therefore plays no role in natural clouds.






WarningKeep S and s apart



“1% supersaturation” means \(S=1.01\) and \(\ln S\approx0.01\); \(\ln 1=0\) only at \(S=1\) (saturation). The requirement for homogeneous nucleation should likewise be written with all three notations kept distinct: \(S\approx4\)–5, i.e. RH 400–500%, i.e. \(s\approx\) 300–400%.

title: From One CCN to a Raindrop: Warm-Cloud Microphysics
section: 2. Aerosol changes the starting point: the Raoult effect and the Köhler curve
text:
2. Aerosol changes the starting point: the Raoult effect and the Köhler curve
Real cloud droplets form by heterogeneous nucleation, as water collects on aerosol particles. On a wettable particle, the same number of molecules gives a larger radius of curvature, so the Kelvin barrier is easier to cross. If the particle dissolves, the equilibrium vapour pressure over the solution drops below that over pure water (the Raoult effect), which helps further. The textbook therefore concludes that the first droplets form on the largest and most soluble CCN. Combining both effects, the equilibrium vapour density at the drop surface is
\[
\begin{aligned}
\rho_v(R) &= \rho_{vs}[T(R)]\left(1+\frac{\hat a}{R}-\frac{\hat b}{R^3}\right) \\
\hat a &= \frac{2\sigma_{vl}}{\rho_L R_v T}, \qquad \hat b = \frac{3 i_{vH} m_s M_w}{4\pi\rho_L M_s}
\end{aligned} \tag{3.18–3.20}
\]
In words: “vapour in equilibrium at the drop surface = saturation value over flat pure water × (1 + curvature correction − solute correction).” \(\hat a/R\) is the Kelvin term, larger for smaller drops; \(\hat b/R^3\) is the Raoult term, larger for more dissolved salt mass \(m_s\), more ions per molecule (van’t Hoff factor \(i_{vH}\)) and lighter salt molecules (molecular weight \(M_s\)). As the drop grows the solution dilutes and the term falls off as \(R^3\).
Plotting the equilibrium saturation ratio \(S_{eq}(R)\approx 1+\hat a/R-\hat b/R^3\) gives the Köhler curve. At small \(R\) the solute term wins and the drop exists as a haze droplet with \(S_{eq}<1\); at large \(R\) the curvature term remains and \(S_{eq}\) is slightly above 1. Setting \(dS_{eq}/dR=0\) gives the maximum at \(R_c=\sqrt{3\hat b/\hat a}\), \(s_c=\sqrt{4\hat a^3/(27\hat b)}\). If the ambient supersaturation exceeds this critical supersaturation \(s_c\), the drop passes \(R_c\) and keeps growing: this is activation. In κ-Köhler theory a dilute solution has \(\hat b\approx\kappa r_d^3\), so \(s_c \propto r_d^{-3/2}\kappa^{-1/2}\). The full form is in my κ-Köhler review (Petters and Kreidenweis 2007).

A tenfold larger dry radius lowers \(s_c\) about thirtyfold, while doubling κ only multiplies \(s_c\) by about 0.7. Within this range size controls activation more strongly than chemistry. A giant CCN of 1 µm radius has \(s_c\) of order 0.001% and activates in practically any cloud, but its \(R_c\) is tens of micrometres, so it is more useful to ask “how quickly does it reach collector size” than “does it activate”.

title: From One CCN to a Raindrop: Warm-Cloud Microphysics
section: 3. Condensational growth: small drops grow fast, large drops slowly
text:
3. Condensational growth: small drops grow fast, large drops slowly
Activated drops grow by vapour diffusion (Fick’s law). Combining steady, spherically symmetric diffusion with a heat balance gives, for a near-saturated environment, the mass growth rate
\[
\begin{aligned}
\dot m &= \frac{4\pi R\, s}{F_\kappa + F_D} \\
F_\kappa &= \frac{L^2}{\kappa_a R_v T^2}, \qquad F_D = \frac{R_v T}{D_v e_s}
\end{aligned} \tag{3.14–3.17}
\]
In words: “mass growth rate = \(4\pi R\) × supersaturation ÷ (heat-conduction resistance + vapour-diffusion resistance).” \(s\) is the driving force. \(F_\kappa\) expresses that the latent heat (\(L\)) released by condensation warms the drop and raises its surface saturation vapour pressure, so the heat must be conducted away through the air (\(\kappa_a\)); \(F_D\) expresses that vapour has to diffuse through the air (\(D_v\)) to reach the drop. Switching from mass to radius (\(m=\tfrac43\pi R^3\rho_L\)),
\[
R\frac{dR}{dt}=\frac{s}{\rho_L(F_\kappa+F_D)}\equiv G\,s \quad\Longrightarrow\quad R^2 = R_0^2 + 2Gs\,t .
\]
Some textbooks fold \(\rho_L\) into the \(F\) terms and write \(R\,dR/dt=(S-1)/(F_k+F_d)\). The key is \(dR/dt = Gs/R\): the larger the drop, the slower its radius grows. Small drops catch up with large ones, so condensation narrows the size distribution. For very small drops the curvature and solute terms must be kept (Eq. 3.21), and for falling drops a ventilation factor multiplies the rate (Eqs. 3.22–3.23).



Radius of a drop growing by condensation alone at s = 0.5%. Curves from different starting sizes quickly converge.

title: From One CCN to a Raindrop: Warm-Cloud Microphysics
text:
4. Fall speed and collision–coalescence
Cloud droplets (under 100 µm in diameter) fall slower than 1 m s⁻¹. Fall speed grows almost linearly with radius up to 500 µm, then more slowly, and levels off near 3 mm radius as the drop flattens into a horizontal disc. Drops of different sizes fall at different speeds and overtake one another. For one large drop falling through cloud droplets, the continuous collection equation is
\[
\begin{aligned}
\dot m_{col} &= A_m\,\lvert V(m)-V(m')\rvert\,\rho q_{m'}\,\Sigma_c(m,m') \\
A_m &= \pi(R+R')^2
\end{aligned} \tag{3.24–3.25}
\]
In words: “collection growth rate = volume swept per second (cross-section × relative fall speed) × cloud-water mass in that volume × fraction that actually sticks.” \(A_m\) is the effective cross-section based on the sum of the radii, the absolute value reflects that only relative motion matters, and \(\rho q_{m'}\) is the cloud liquid water content (g m⁻³). The collection efficiency \(\Sigma_c\) is collision efficiency × coalescence efficiency. Collision efficiency is below 1 when the airflow around the large drop carries small droplets aside, and can exceed 1 when droplets are pulled into its wake. Coalescence efficiency is the fraction of colliding pairs that actually merge; models often set it to 1, but in heavy rain colliding drops may stay together only briefly.
For \(R\gg R'\), \(A_m\approx\pi R^2\) and \(m=\tfrac43\pi R^3\rho_L\), so \(dR/dt\approx\Sigma_c\lvert\Delta V\rvert\rho q_c/(4\rho_L)\). Unlike condensation, growth speeds up as the drop gets larger, because fall speed and collision efficiency both increase. The problem is getting started. Reading the textbook’s Fig. 3.5 (collision efficiencies from Wallace & Hobbs) by eye, a 10 µm-radius collector reaches a collision efficiency of at most about 0.05, a 20 µm collector about 0.2, and only collectors of 40 µm or more approach 0.7–1. Real collection is not continuous but probabilistic, so drops starting at the same size diverge as some happen to collide first (stochastic collection, Eqs. 3.27–3.33). In the example calculation the textbook shows, after about 30 minutes cloud droplets near 10 µm radius still dominate by number, but a large part of the water mass has moved into raindrops near 1 mm radius.

radius of a few µm or less
collector radius of tens of µm or more



Between about 10 µm and a few tens of µm in radius, condensation has already slowed and collision efficiency is still small. How quickly drops cross this gap sets the onset of warm rain. The two hygroscopic seeding approaches summarized by Bruintjes (1999) target exactly this gap.

Embryo approach: salt particles larger than 10 µm in diameter supply collector candidates from the start, jumping the gap.
Flare approach: salt particles of about 0.5 µm diameter are released below cloud base. The large artificial CCN activate first and take up vapour, fewer natural CCN activate, and fewer droplets grow larger. This changes the competition for vapour.

The \(R^2\propto t\) figure suggests one more point. Drops starting at 2 µm and 5 µm are almost the same size after 20 minutes. A slightly larger starting size is therefore quickly forgotten; my reading of the equation is that inserting drops near collector size, or reducing the number of competitors, is what makes the difference. Conversely, if small hygroscopic particles add droplets instead of replacing natural CCN, rain could be delayed. Ren et al. (2025), which I read later, reported for one convective case in a two-dimensional bin model that, at a fixed seeding mass, particles of 0.1–0.9 µm diameter suppressed precipitation and the response turned to enhancement above about 2 µm diameter (Ren et al. 2025). This question continues in my 0-D reproduction of Ren (2025).

title: Microphysics Scheme Comparison and the Fast SBM 2-D Aerosol Reset Bug
text: Lin, used in the previous post, is a single-moment scheme with no droplet number and no CCN, so it cannot represent an experiment that “changes the aerosol size distribution”, such as hygroscopic seeding. Seeding needs bin microphysics with aerosol bins, so I chose WRF’s fast SBM (mp_physics = 30). First, I ran the same squall line with Lin → Morrison → fast SBM to see how the schemes differ, and finally changed only the fast SBM background aerosol to maritime. Along the way I hit a bug that appears only when fast SBM is used in 2-D.

title: Microphysics Scheme Comparison and the Fast SBM 2-D Aerosol Reset Bug
section: Problem 1: stopping at 15 min with dt 3 s
text:
Problem 1: stopping at 15 min with dt 3 s
rsl.error.0000 simply stopped at model time 00:15:33; the error was only in rank 1’s log rsl.error.0001 (the region where the cloud was growing): fatal error in ONECOND1-in (ABS(DAL1*DELMASSL1) > 3.0). The check in the source means:
\[\Delta T = \frac{L}{c_p}\,\Delta q_l, \qquad |\Delta T| > 3\ \mathrm{K} \;\Rightarrow\; \text{stop}\]
Multiplying the change in liquid mixing ratio from one condensation step, \(\Delta q_l\), by latent heat \(L\) divided by the specific heat at constant pressure \(c_p\) gives the warming \(\Delta T\) of the air from that condensation. If it exceeds 3 K in one step, the scheme treats the calculation as untrustworthy and stops itself. In a strong updraft a long time step lumps too much condensation into one step, so I reduced dt to 2 s and the run finished. I did not re-test 3 s after the patch below, so I do not know whether this error was related to the reset bug.

title: Microphysics Scheme Comparison and the Fast SBM 2-D Aerosol Reset Bug
section: Problem 2: it finished, but no rain — the 2-D aerosol reset bug
text:
Problem 2: it finished, but no rain — the 2-D aerosol reset bug
With dt 2 s the run reached the end, but the result was strange, and there was not a single error.



Symptom (before patch)
Value




Surface rain, rain water
zero for 60 min


Max cloud water
flat at 13.5 g/kg


Droplet number
~30,000 cm⁻³ (normally a few hundred)


Drop size
all at 2–6 µm radius


Aerosol at 0–1 km (30 → 60 min)
1774 → 1775 cm⁻³, not consumed






Comparison before the patch. FastSBM (green, dt 2 s) has max cloud water flat near 13.5 g/kg and zero rain water and surface rain. The Lin and Morrison lines in this figure are dt 3 s runs, so read only the green line.


Once rain forms, aerosol below cloud should decrease through activation and scavenging, but it stayed constant. Something was refilling the aerosol every step. I found the cause in phys/module_mp_fast_sbm.F (WRF 4.6.0, around line ~4320).
! when itimestep > 1 and domain_id == 1 (in my source, a block compiled only for MPI builds)
if (i <= 5 .or. i >= IDE-5 .OR. &
    & j <= 5 .or. j >= JDE-5)THEN
   ! reset the aerosol bins (ff8i) to the initial distribution
This is a lateral boundary condition that keeps supplying aerosol to the outer 5 cells of a 3-D real-case domain. In the 2-D setup, however, e_sn = 10, so \(JDE = 10\) and \(JDE - 5 = 5\). Every y row j = 1–9 satisfies “j ≤ 5 or j ≥ 5”, so the aerosol of the whole domain is reset to its initial value every step. Working through the condition, any setup with e_sn of 11 or less is affected. With aerosol refilled without limit, new droplets kept forming; water shared among tens of thousands of droplets could not grow by collision–coalescence into rain. For seeding it is even worse: seeding particles placed in ff8i are overwritten at the next step.
The patch turns off only the y condition and keeps the aerosol supply at the open x boundaries.
cp phys/module_mp_fast_sbm.F phys/module_mp_fast_sbm.F.orig
sed -i 's/& j <= 5 .or. j >= JDE-5)THEN/\& .false.)THEN   ! 2D patch: y-edge aerosol reset off (e_sn=10)/' phys/module_mp_fast_sbm.F
./compile em_quarter_ss > compile_fsbm_patch.log 2>&1

This patch is a local change applied only to my working copy of WRF 4.6.0, not to the lab’s original WRF installation, and I checked it only in this 2-D setup with e_sn = 10. It is not an official fix, and I have not looked at the source of other versions. If you see the same symptoms (no errors, zero rain, tens of thousands of droplets per cm³, aerosol that never decreases), this condition is a good first place to look.

The difference is already large at 10 min, when convection is just starting, so I treat it as numerical rather than chaotic noise (which process is responsible is still unknown). Two lessons: compare experiments at the same dt, and check convergence once by reducing dt when using a new setup. And a seeding effect is meaningful only if it is clearly larger than numerical sensitivity like this.
Morrison makes rain aloft later. Max rain water at 10 min is about 1 g/kg for Lin and almost zero for Morrison (surface onset falls in the same 10-min window). I think the explanation lies in the autoconversion formula; WRF’s Morrison scheme uses the Khairoutdinov–Kogan form (Khairoutdinov and Kogan 2000).
\[P_{aut} = 1350\, q_c^{2.47}\, N_c^{-1.79}\]
The rate \(P_{aut}\) at which cloud droplets first merge into raindrops grows with the 2.47 power of the cloud water mixing ratio \(q_c\) (kg/kg) and falls with the −1.79 power of droplet number concentration \(N_c\) (cm⁻³). When the same cloud water is shared by more droplets, each droplet is smaller and converts to rain less easily. The fixed \(N_c\) = 250 cm⁻³ appears to delay the first rain, but I did not break it down process by process.
Fast SBM rains less and later. Its default background aerosol is continental (~1760 cm⁻³ at 0–1 km), so droplets are many and small. Cloud water piles up to 10.7 g/kg at 20 min, and rain reaches the ground only at 30–40 min. If this interpretation is right, reducing only the aerosol should make rain earlier and heavier.

title: Microphysics Scheme Comparison and the Fast SBM 2-D Aerosol Reset Bug
section: L3.5: changing only the background aerosol to maritime
text:
L3.5: changing only the background aerosol to maritime
Fast SBM chooses its aerosol distribution from the grid’s surface type (XLAND: 1 = land → continental, 2 = sea → maritime). At first I changed XLAND in wrfinput_d01 to 2 after ideal.exe, but the result table and figure files were byte-for-byte identical to the continental run. The reason: wrf.exe overwrites XLAND at startup with the namelist value ideal_xland (default 1). I added ideal_xland = 2 to &physics and confirmed it with grep -i ideal_xland namelist.output. When two experiments are completely identical, suspect “the setting never got in” before “no effect”, because convection amplifies even tiny differences.







Continental → maritime
Value

Droplet number (10 / 20 / 30 min)
438 / 341 / 292 → 47 / 28 / 39 cm⁻³


Drop mass mode at 10 min (radius)

Max rain water at 10 min

60-min domain-mean rain

Continental fast SBM: (a) drop mass distribution, (b) number distribution, (c) aerosol distribution at 0–1 km. The x-axis is radius.





The same figure for maritime fast SBM. The 10-min cloud mode sits at a larger radius and the raindrop mode grows earlier.


aerosol ↓ → droplet number ↓ (~1/10) → each droplet larger (13 → 20 µm)
  → collision–coalescence starts earlier → rain aloft from 10 min → surface rain earlier and heavier
The 0 cm⁻³ aerosol at 00:00 in the size-distribution figures appears to be because the bins are not yet filled in the initial output, so I used only the 30- and 60-min values. Even the maritime run produces less surface rain than Lin. Why it has plenty of rain aloft but less at the ground (evaporation below cloud, or ice processes?) is still unresolved.






NoteAddendum (checked in late October): y rows differ slightly



Although the runs are 2-D, fast SBM rain differed slightly between y rows (60-min domain mean: continental 1.34–1.42 mm, maritime 2.21–2.40 mm). Lin and Morrison show zero difference between rows. Reading the source, the likely cause is a part of the ice-process block that treats the last y row as the “domain edge” and computes the wind average differently there — the same kind of “3-D real-case assumption” as the reset bug. I have only proposed a patch; no confirmation run yet. So all comparisons above use the average over all y rows, and point maxima are given with their row range. The row-to-row spread (about ±3–4 %) is far smaller than the continental → maritime difference (+66 %).



Conclusion. On the same squall line, fast SBM (continental) produced about 60 % less rain than Lin and Morrison, and later; switching only the background aerosol to maritime increased rain about 1.7-fold and made it earlier. The model responds to aerosol changes — but only after turning off the condition that reset aerosol every step in 2-D, and scheme comparisons were meaningful only at the same dt.

text:
Geresdi et al. (2020)은 Wyoming Weather Modification Pilot Project의 실제 네 사례를 3차원 WRF와 bin 미세물리 모형으로 다시 계산했다 (Geresdi 기타 2020년). 질문은 단순하다. 지상에서 방출한 AgI가 산악 구름 안으로 들어갔을 때, 어떤 조건에서 실제 지상 강수 증가까지 이어지는가?
원문 보기

title: 산악 구름 씨뿌리기에서 중요한 것은 투입량보다 ‘겹침’이다
text:
연구가 풀려는 문제
빙정핵 씨뿌리기의 개념적 사슬은 익숙하다. AgI가 얼음핵으로 활성화되고, 빙정 수가 늘고, 수증기 증착과 착빙으로 입자가 성장해 눈이나 비가 된다. 그러나 실제 산악 지형에서는 바람, 경계층 난류, 지형에 따른 상승류가 AgI 플룸을 계속 변형한다. 구름 속 액체수도 균일하지 않다. 사슬의 한 단계라도 끊기면 지상 강수 증가는 나타나지 않는다.
이 연구는 네 실험 단위(RSE023, RSE077, RSE114, RSE149)에 대해 자연 구름을 모의한 CTRL과 AgI를 투입한 SEED를 비교했다. 실제 지형과 지상 발생기 위치를 사용하고, University of Pécs–NCAR bin 미세물리 모형으로 수상체 스펙트럼과 미세물리 전환을 추적했다.

title: 산악 구름 씨뿌리기에서 중요한 것은 투입량보다 ‘겹침’이다
text:
왜 3차원 계산이 필요한가
2차원 단면 모의에서는 물질이 옆 방향으로 빠져나갈 수 없다. 3차원에서는 지형과 난류가 AgI를 수평·연직으로 동시에 퍼뜨린다. 같은 방출률이어도 3차원 플룸의 최대 농도가 2차원보다 대략 한 자릿수 낮아질 수 있다는 것이 핵심이다. 즉, 2차원에서 효과가 커 보였던 설정이 실제 산악 지형에서는 희석될 수 있다.
반대로 3차원 지형은 단순히 효과를 약화시키기만 하는 것이 아니다. 계곡과 사면을 따라 형성된 흐름이 플룸을 과냉각 구름으로 운반할 수도 있다. 따라서 발생기 위치는 “산 위인가 아래인가”보다 방출된 입자가 어느 유선을 따라 액체수 영역과 만나는가로 평가해야 한다.

title: 산악 구름 씨뿌리기에서 중요한 것은 투입량보다 ‘겹침’이다
text:
핵심 진단량: 수평 액체수 경로
저자들은 바람 방향을 따라 구름 속 액체수를 적분한 수평 액체수 경로(horizontal liquid water path, h-LWP)를 제안한다. 비행기가 연직으로 측정하는 LWP와 달리, 씨뿌리기 물질과 성장 중인 입자가 실제로 지나가는 경로에 얼마나 많은 액체수가 있는지를 나타낸다.

연구가 제안한 h-LWP 해석 범위


최대 h-LWP
모의에서 나타난 경향




\(<0.1\ \mathrm{mm}\)
강수 증강이 거의 없음


약 \(0.5\ \mathrm{mm}\) 이상
5% 안팎의 유의미한 증강이 가능해짐


\(>1.0\ \mathrm{mm}\)
성장 시간이 확보되면 더 뚜렷한 증강 가능



이 수치는 보편적인 임계값이라기보다 네 사례에서 얻은 경험적 진단 기준이다. 그럼에도 “구름에 액체수가 있다”는 정성적 설명을 “플룸이 따라가는 경로에 성장 가능한 물이 얼마나 있는가”라는 검증 가능한 질문으로 바꿔 준다.

title: 산악 구름 씨뿌리기에서 중요한 것은 투입량보다 ‘겹침’이다
text:
미세물리 사슬을 따라 읽기
SEED 실험에서는 먼저 pristine ice가 늘고 수증기 증착이 강해졌다. 이후 응집과 착빙이 작동하면서 눈 입자가 커졌다. 지상 강수 증가와 가장 일관되게 연결된 과정은 눈의 확산 성장과 착빙이었다.
하지만 초기에 새 빙정이 너무 많은 액체수를 빠르게 소모하면 이후 성장에 필요한 물이 부족해질 수 있다. “빙정 수 증가” 자체는 성공 지표가 아니다. 최종적으로 큰 입자가 되어 지표에 도달했는지, 그리고 그 과정에서 구름의 물 수지가 어떻게 바뀌었는지를 함께 봐야 한다.

title: 산악 구름 씨뿌리기에서 중요한 것은 투입량보다 ‘겹침’이다
section: 이 논문이 보여준 것과 보여주지 못한 것
text:
이 논문이 보여준 것과 보여주지 못한 것
보여준 것은 실제 지형, 플룸 수송, 과냉각 액체수, 미세물리 성장 과정이 하나의 연쇄로 연결되어야 한다는 점이다. 발생기 재배치만으로 효과가 달라진 사례도 있어 공간적 겹침의 중요성이 분명하다.
아직 보여주지 못한 것은 통계적으로 일반화 가능한 효과 크기다. 사례가 네 개뿐이고 결과가 사례별 구름 구조에 민감하다. 모형의 자연 강수 오차와 빙정핵 활성화 가정도 CTRL–SEED 차이에 영향을 준다. 이 논문은 “몇 퍼센트 늘어난다”는 보편식을 주기보다, 성공과 실패를 판별할 물리적 체크리스트를 준다.

title: 산악 구름 씨뿌리기에서 중요한 것은 투입량보다 ‘겹침’이다
text:
PySDM·WRF 실험으로 가져갈 질문

투입 입자 수를 고정하고 액체수 경로와 체류시간만 바꾸면 성장 스펙트럼은 어떻게 달라지는가?
AgI 플룸과 과냉각 액체수의 겹침을 하나의 지표로 만들 수 있는가?
빙정 수 증가, 눈 질량 증가, 지상 강수 증가 사이의 시간 지연을 어떻게 추적할 것인가?
2차원과 3차원 수송 차이가 씨뿌리기 효율을 얼마나 과대평가하게 만드는가?

가장 중요한 교훈은 효과량보다 과정의 폐쇄성이다. 씨뿌리기 물질이 구름에 들어갔다는 사실과 지상 강수가 늘었다는 결론 사이를, 수송–핵생성–성장–낙하의 증거로 채워야 한다.

title: 산악 구름 씨뿌리기에서 중요한 것은 투입량보다 ‘겹침’이다
text:
참고문헌


Geresdi, István, Lulin Xue, Noémi Sarkadi, 와/과 Roy Rasmussen. 2020년. “Evaluation of Orographic Cloud Seeding Using a Bin Microphysics Scheme: Three-Dimensional Simulation of Real Cases”. Journal of Applied Meteorology and Climatology 59 (9): 1537–53. https://doi.org/10.1175/JAMC-D-19-0278.1.

title: 음이온으로 비를 늘릴 수 있을까: 중국 첫 현장시험 다시 읽기
text:
Zheng et al. (2021)은 중국 Wushaoling과 Liupan Mountains에서 고전압 코로나 방전으로 음이온을 발생시킨 뒤 강수와 구름 변화를 평가했다 (Zheng 기타 2021년). 논문은 중국 최초의 음이온 기반 야외 강우 증강 시험이라는 점과, 서로 다른 일곱 분석을 한꺼번에 사용했다는 점에서 눈에 띈다.
원문 보기

title: 음이온으로 비를 늘릴 수 있을까: 중국 첫 현장시험 다시 읽기
text:
제안된 물리 가설
장치는 지상에서 고전압 코로나 방전으로 많은 음이온을 만든다. 주변 에어로졸이 음전하를 띠고, 바람과 상승류를 따라 구름으로 이동해 응결핵 또는 충돌·병합 과정에 영향을 준다는 가설이다. AgI나 흡습성 염을 직접 살포하는 방식과 달리, 생성 지점과 실제 구름 반응 지점 사이의 수송과 전하 유지가 핵심 연결고리다.
논문이 성공을 주장하려면 최소한 세 단계가 모두 확인되어야 한다.

장치 단계: 발전기가 충분한 음이온을 만들었는가?
구름 단계: 이온 또는 대전 입자가 구름에 도달해 미세물리를 바꿨는가?
강수 단계: 그 변화가 자연 변동을 넘어 강수 증가로 이어졌는가?

title: 음이온으로 비를 늘릴 수 있을까: 중국 첫 현장시험 다시 읽기
text:
현장 설계와 일곱 분석
Wushaoling에서는 2020년 7–11월 중 14일 ON, 13일 OFF를 무작위로 운영했다. Liupan에서는 장치를 주로 연속 가동했고 네트워크 장애 기간을 비교 자료로 사용해 대조 설계가 더 약하다. 저자들은 짧은 자료의 한계를 보완하기 위해 다음 분석을 함께 제시했다.

신경망으로 예측한 무처리 강수와 실제 강수 비교
과거 기후자료의 전·후반기 강수비 비교
ON/OFF 무작위 일자 비교
주변 관측소의 지리적 보간
풍상·풍하측 강수 비교
발전기 주변 음이온 농도 비교
전천카메라의 구름량·구름두께 비교

title: 음이온으로 비를 늘릴 수 있을까: 중국 첫 현장시험 다시 읽기
text:
결과를 증거의 강도로 나누기

1. 장치가 작동했다는 증거
발전기 가동 시 주변 음이온 농도 차이는 매우 작은 p값으로 나타났다. 이 결과는 장치가 지상 관측 지점의 전기적 환경을 바꿨다는 강한 증거다. 그러나 지상 음이온 증가가 곧 구름 내부 농도 증가를 뜻하지는 않는다.


2. 구름이 달라졌다는 간접 증거
전천카메라 분석에서는 일부 월의 총운량과 얇은·두꺼운 구름 비율이 증가했고, 몇 비교에서 \(p<0.02\)가 보고됐다. 이는 흥미로운 중간 증거지만, 대전 입자의 연직 분포와 구름방울 크기분포를 직접 측정하지 않았기 때문에 미세물리 경로는 여전히 추론이다.


3. 비가 늘었다는 증거
기계학습 비교에서는 실제 평균 강수가 예측값보다 약 21% 많았다. 풍하측 강수는 풍상측보다 Wushaoling에서 약 58%, Liupan에서 약 19% 높게 계산됐다. 그러나 주요 강수 비교의 p값은 각각 약 0.29–0.46 범위로, 일반적인 유의수준에서 귀무가설을 기각하지 못했다. 과거 계절성 비교도 같은 문제를 갖는다.
즉, 관측된 방향은 연구 가설과 일치하지만 표본이 작고 자연 강수 변동이 커서 효과 크기의 불확실성이 넓다.

title: 음이온으로 비를 늘릴 수 있을까: 중국 첫 현장시험 다시 읽기
section: 여러 분석이 자동으로 강한 증거가 되지는 않는다
text:
여러 분석이 자동으로 강한 증거가 되지는 않는다
일곱 방법이 모두 비슷한 방향을 가리킨다는 점은 장점이다. 하지만 분석들이 같은 4개월 자료와 같은 기상 사건을 공유하므로 서로 완전히 독립적이지 않다. 같은 자연 변동이 여러 지표에 반복해서 나타날 수 있다. 2020년의 특이한 기후 상태, 관측소 위치, 장치 가동 시기의 차이도 결과를 설명할 수 있다.
특히 신경망의 높은 적합도는 반사실적 강수, 즉 “그날 장치를 끄면 얼마가 왔을까”를 정확히 안다는 보장이 아니다. 예측 모형이 학습하지 못한 2020년의 기상 편향이 효과로 흡수될 수 있다.

title: 음이온으로 비를 늘릴 수 있을까: 중국 첫 현장시험 다시 읽기
text:
더 강한 다음 실험
후속 연구라면 다음을 우선하고 싶다.

여러 시즌에 걸친 사전등록 무작위 ON/OFF 설계
운영자도 모르는 블라인드 스케줄과 독립 분석
라디오존데·드론·항공기로 이온과 대전 에어로졸의 연직 수송 직접 관측
구름방울 수농도와 크기분포, 액체수량의 동시 측정
강수량 하나가 아니라 장치→수송→미세물리→강수의 매개 경로 분석

이 논문을 “음이온 씨뿌리기가 20% 효과가 있다”로 요약하면 과도하다. 더 정확한 독해는 이렇다. 장치 작동과 일부 구름 지표 변화는 관측됐고, 강수 증가 방향도 나타났지만, 짧은 기간과 약한 대조 설계 때문에 강수 인과효과는 아직 확정되지 않았다.

title: 음이온으로 비를 늘릴 수 있을까: 중국 첫 현장시험 다시 읽기
text:
참고문헌


Zheng, Wei, Hengben Ma, Ming Zhang, 기타. 2021년. “Evaluation of the First Negative Ion-Based Cloud Seeding and Rain Enhancement Trial in China”. Water 13 (18): 2473. https://doi.org/10.3390/w13182473.

title: WRF로 묻는 흡습성 씨뿌리기의 최적 고도와 면적
text:
Lin et al. (2023)은 WRF의 WDM6 bulk 미세물리에 43개 CCN 크기 bin을 결합한 WDM6–NCU 모형을 개발하고, 2020년 10월 대만의 층적운 사례에서 흡습성 씨뿌리기 민감도를 계산했다 (Lin 기타 2023년). “입자를 많이 뿌리면 비가 늘어난다”가 아니라, 어디에·얼마나 넓게·어떤 크기로 뿌려야 하는가를 묻는 연구다.
원문 보기

title: WRF로 묻는 흡습성 씨뿌리기의 최적 고도와 면적
text:
왜 혼합 미세물리인가
bulk 모형은 계산이 빠르지만 씨뿌리기 입자의 세밀한 크기분포를 직접 추적하기 어렵다. 완전한 bin 모형은 풍부한 정보를 주지만 실사례 고해상도 WRF에서 비용이 크다. 저자들은 WDM6의 구름·비 과정은 유지하고, CCN 반지름 \(0.001\)–\(20\ \mu\mathrm{m}\)를 43개 bin으로 나눠 활성화를 계산했다.
초기 살포입자 분포는 실제 cloud seeding rocket device(CSRD) flare의 삼봉형 분포를 사용했다. 따라서 단일 평균반지름으로 처리하는 것보다 큰 입자와 작은 입자의 역할을 나누어 볼 수 있다.

title: WRF로 묻는 흡습성 씨뿌리기의 최적 고도와 면적
text:
실험 구성
WRF 3.9.1의 중첩 격자를 사용했고, 가장 안쪽 영역은 333 m 간격의 LES 설정이다. 실제 구름 사례를 재현한 뒤 다음 조건을 바꿨다.

살포 고도: 500, 1000, 1300, 2200 m
살포 면적: 1, 10, 36, 64, 100 km²
입자 농도와 크기 구간
씨뿌리기 유무

1300 m는 구름 내부, 500 m는 구름 밑 조건을 대표한다. 각 실험에서 강수량뿐 아니라 CCN 활성화, 구름방울과 빗방울 수·질량, 미세물리 생성률을 비교했다.

title: WRF로 묻는 흡습성 씨뿌리기의 최적 고도와 면적
text:
결과 1: 구름 안 살포가 유리했다
이 사례에서는 1300 m 살포가 가장 효과적이었다. 구름 내부의 높은 과포화도와 액체수 때문에 입자가 빠르게 활성화되고 방울 성장에 참여할 수 있었다. 500 m 살포에서는 입자가 구름 밑에서 이동하는 동안 희석되고, 구름에 들어가더라도 최적 영역과의 겹침이 약했다.
저자들은 이 층운 사례의 목표 영역으로 과포화도 0.5% 초과, 액체수량 \(0.6\ \mathrm{g\,m^{-3}}\) 초과인 구름 내부를 제안한다. 액체수 기준은 선행연구의 \(0.5\ \mathrm{g\,m^{-3}}\)와 비슷하지만, 한 사례에서 얻은 값이므로 다른 구름 체계에 그대로 적용하기보다 탐색 지표로 사용해야 한다.

title: WRF로 묻는 흡습성 씨뿌리기의 최적 고도와 면적
WRF로 묻는 흡습성 씨뿌리기의 최적 고도와 면적
text:
결과 3: 핵심 과정은 accretion이었다
흡습성 입자는 CCN으로 활성화되어 방울 스펙트럼을 바꿨다. 구름 밑 살포에서는 autoconversion 증가가 일부 보였지만, 전체 강수 증가를 가장 잘 설명한 과정은 빗방울이 구름방울을 쓸어 모으는 accretion(\(P_{racw}\)) 강화였다. 이미 형성된 빗방울이 충분한 구름물을 만날 때 질량 증가가 가속된 것이다.
입자 크기별로는 반지름 약 \(0.4\ \mu\mathrm{m}\)보다 큰 살포입자의 기여가 컸다. 그러나 큰 입자만 무한히 늘리면 giant CCN 경쟁과 제한된 액체수 때문에 다른 반응이 나타날 수 있다. 실제 최적 분포는 구름의 배경 CCN과 상승류에 의존한다.

title: WRF로 묻는 흡습성 씨뿌리기의 최적 고도와 면적
text:
연구의 한계

실제 한 층적운 사례에 대한 결과라 보편성이 없다.
bin CCN이 활성화된 뒤 bulk 수상체로 합쳐져 세부 크기분포 정보가 일부 사라진다.
살포 플룸의 실제 난류 확산과 입자 성장 가정에 불확실성이 있다.
모의 CTRL–SEED 차이는 물리 가설의 가능성을 보이지만 현장 강수 증강을 입증하는 관측은 아니다.
최적 고도·면적은 구름 깊이, 배경 에어로졸, LWC, 상승류가 달라지면 함께 변한다.

title: WRF로 묻는 흡습성 씨뿌리기의 최적 고도와 면적
text:
다음 WRF·PySDM 실험
WRF에서는 여러 구름 사례와 물리 조합으로 40–60 km² 포화가 유지되는지 앙상블을 만들 수 있다. PySDM에서는 같은 상승류 궤적을 사용해 CSRD 크기분포의 각 모드가 활성화와 충돌·병합에 기여하는 정도를 더 세밀하게 분리할 수 있다.
특히 다음 세 지도를 함께 만들고 싶다.

씨뿌리기 입자 농도와 체류시간
과포화도·액체수량의 목표 가능 영역
accretion 증가와 지상 강수 반응

세 지도가 겹치는 위치가 실제 살포 목표가 된다. 이 논문의 가장 좋은 점은 “많이 뿌리기”를 최적화 문제가 아니라 구름물이 있는 곳에서 성장 과정을 여는 배치 문제로 바꾼 데 있다.

title: WRF로 묻는 흡습성 씨뿌리기의 최적 고도와 면적
text:
참고문헌


Lin, Kai-I, Kao-Shen Chung, Sheng-Hsiang Wang, 기타. 2023년. “Evaluation of Hygroscopic Cloud Seeding in Warm-Rain Processes by a Hybrid Microphysics Scheme Using a Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) Model: A Real Case Study”. Atmospheric Chemistry and Physics 23: 10423–38. https://doi.org/10.5194/acp-23-10423-2023.

title: PySDM 실험 스크립트를 하나의 Seeding Lab으로 만들기
text:
PySDM으로 구름 씨뿌리기 민감도 실험을 시작할 때 가장 먼저 부딪힌 문제는 미세물리식이 아니었다. 실험 조건을 바꿀 때마다 Python 파일을 직접 수정하고, 결과 폴더 이름을 기억하고, 어떤 설정으로 만든 그림인지 다시 추적해야 했다. 계산은 실행되지만 연구 과정은 쉽게 재현되지 않았다.
2026년 7월 13일 병합한 PySDM-Seeding-Lab PR #2는 이 문제를 해결하기 위해 스크립트 모음을 시나리오 기반 실험 플랫폼으로 바꾼 첫 단계다. 31개 커밋과 66개 변경 파일에는 기능 추가뿐 아니라, 실험을 하나의 추적 가능한 단위로 만들기 위한 시행착오가 담겨 있다.

title: PySDM 실험 스크립트를 하나의 Seeding Lab으로 만들기
section: 출발점: 실행은 되지만 실험은 남지 않았다
text:
출발점: 실행은 되지만 실험은 남지 않았다
초기의 작업 방식은 단순했다. 설정값을 수정하고 스크립트를 실행한 뒤 CSV와 그림을 확인했다. 한두 번의 테스트에는 충분했지만 조건 수가 늘자 문제가 빠르게 커졌다.

어떤 실험에서 사용한 설정인지 결과만 보고 알기 어려웠다.
기준 실험과 씨뿌리기 실험의 차이를 수작업으로 맞춰야 했다.
건조반지름, \(\kappa\), 주입 시각을 동시에 바꾸면 실행 수를 놓치기 쉬웠다.
같은 실험을 다시 실행해도 결과 폴더와 그림을 연결하기 어려웠다.
긴 sweep 도중 어디까지 진행됐는지 알 수 없었다.

여기서 목표를 “GUI를 만든다”가 아니라 하나의 과학 질문을 하나의 시나리오로 보존한다로 정했다.

title: PySDM 실험 스크립트를 하나의 Seeding Lab으로 만들기
text:
Scenario를 실험의 기본 단위로
새로운 흐름은 다음과 같이 설계했다.
Create scenario
→ configure environment / aerosol / seeding / dynamics
→ configure parameter sweep
→ run simulation
→ inspect results through dashboard
시나리오는 이름, 짧은 메모, 생성 시각과 전체 설정을 YAML로 저장한다.
name: Dry radius and kappa sweep
slug: dry_radius_kappa_sweep
memo: Compare activation response under a fixed updraft
설정 페이지에서 현재 working config뿐 아니라 저장된 시나리오를 직접 선택해 수정할 수 있도록 했다. 결과 폴더에도 시나리오 slug를 넣었다.
results/20260713_XXXXXX_dry_radius_kappa_sweep_parameter_sweep/
이름을 보기 좋게 만드는 기능처럼 보이지만, 실제 목적은 결과에서 원래 실험 설계로 되돌아갈 수 있게 하는 것이다.

title: PySDM 실험 스크립트를 하나의 Seeding Lab으로 만들기
text:
화면 순서를 연구 순서로 바꾸기
Streamlit 페이지는 사용자가 실험을 설계하는 순서와 맞췄다.
00. Experiment Scenarios
01. Atmospheric Environment
02. Background Aerosol Settings
03. Seeding Particle Settings
04. Dynamic Parameters
05. Parameter Sweep
06. Run Simulation
07. Results Dashboard
페이지 번호는 단순한 정렬용 접두사가 아니다. 환경과 배경 에어로졸을 먼저 정의하고, 씨뿌리기 입자와 동역학을 설정한 뒤, 마지막에 변화시킬 변수를 고르게 한다. UI 자체가 실험 설계의 체크리스트가 되도록 한 것이다.

title: PySDM 실험 스크립트를 하나의 Seeding Lab으로 만들기
text:
비교 실험과 parameter sweep
씨뿌리기 효과는 seeding 실행 하나만으로 해석할 수 없다. 동일한 환경에서 기준 실행과 씨뿌리기 실행을 묶는 comparison 모드를 만들었다.
control/
seeding/
comparison.csv
summary.json
metadata.json
config.yaml
각 변수에는 control, seeding, 차이와 상대변화를 함께 저장한다.
\[
\Delta X = X_{seeding}-X_{control}
\]
첫 sweep 카탈로그에는 건조반지름, \(\kappa\), 주입 시작·지속시간, 상승속도, collision ON/OFF를 넣었다. 실행 전에는 다음 곱으로 전체 모델 실행 수를 계산한다.
parameter combinations
× ensemble members
× control/seeding
이 사전 계산은 편의 기능이면서 동시에 안전장치다. 작은 입력 변경이 수백 번의 실행으로 커지는 것을 시작 전에 보여준다.

title: PySDM 실험 스크립트를 하나의 Seeding Lab으로 만들기
text:
결과를 ‘그림’이 아니라 경로로 읽기
Results Dashboard에는 single, comparison, sweep, ensemble 네 종류를 연결했다. 단일 최종값뿐 아니라 다음 성장 경로를 한 화면에서 추적하도록 구성했다.
vapour / supersaturation
→ cloud water response
→ activated particle response
→ size growth
→ rain water response
ensemble에서는 평균±표준편차와 중앙값·사분위범위를 제공하고, sweep에서는 조건 필터와 상대 주입시각 정렬을 추가했다. 특히 많은 조건 중 앞부분만 그리던 문제를 수정해, 표시 수가 제한되어도 전체 sweep 범위에서 사례를 표본화하도록 했다. 그렇지 않으면 뒤쪽의 큰 반지름 조건이 실험에 존재하면서도 그래프에는 나타나지 않을 수 있었다.

title: PySDM 실험 스크립트를 하나의 Seeding Lab으로 만들기
text:
실패 기록 1: Streamlit 경로 충돌
페이지 이름을 재구성한 뒤 이전 파일이 남아 다음 오류가 발생했다.
Multiple Pages specified with URL pathname run
새 파일을 추가하는 것만으로는 충분하지 않았다. 기존 페이지를 일관되게 정리하는 cleanup_old_pages.py를 만들고, 무결성 검사에서 예상 페이지와 중복 파일을 함께 확인하도록 했다.

title: PySDM 실험 스크립트를 하나의 Seeding Lab으로 만들기
section: 실패 기록 2: 실행 중인 CSV를 읽었다
text:
실패 기록 2: 실행 중인 CSV를 읽었다
긴 sweep을 실행하면서 dashboard가 아직 기록 중인 CSV를 읽어 다음 오류가 발생했다.
pandas.errors.EmptyDataError: No columns to parse from file
결과 디렉터리가 존재한다는 사실과 결과가 완성됐다는 사실을 구분해야 했다. 안전한 CSV 읽기와 미완성 결과 필터를 추가했다.
그 과정에서 safe_read_csv()가 실수로 자기 자신을 호출하는 재귀 버그도 생겼다.
# 잘못된 코드
return safe_read_csv(path)

# 수정
return pd.read_csv(path)
단순 hotfix로 끝내지 않고 무결성 검사가 이 패턴을 잡도록 했다. 대시보드 안정성은 예외처리 몇 줄보다 실패가 다시 들어오지 못하게 하는 검사에서 만들어졌다.

title: PySDM 실험 스크립트를 하나의 Seeding Lab으로 만들기
text:
이번 단계에서 얻은 것



이전
PR #2 이후




스크립트마다 설정 수정
YAML Scenario로 질문과 설정 보존


결과 폴더를 수동 추적
Scenario slug와 metadata로 연결


단일 실행 중심
Control–Seeding, sweep, ensemble 지원


최종 그래프 중심
성장경로와 불확실성 진단


진행 상황 확인 어려움
case·member 단위 진행 이벤트



하지만 중요한 한계도 남았다. 일부 성장경로 변수는 PySDM native product가 아니라 제한된 adapter 출력에서 추정한 proxy였다. 플랫폼의 흐름을 검증하는 데는 쓸 수 있지만, 물리 결과로 그대로 해석해서는 안 된다.
이 문제는 다음 개발 단계의 질문이 됐다.

이 결과가 PySDM이 직접 계산한 값인지, 가공한 값인지, 임시 proxy인지 사용자가 어떻게 확인할 수 있을까?

첫 번째 개발은 “실험을 실행할 수 있는 Lab”을 만들었다. 다음 개발은 그 Lab의 결과를 믿을 수 있는 근거를 만드는 작업으로 이어졌다.

title: PySDM 실험 스크립트를 하나의 Seeding Lab으로 만들기
text:
연결 자료

Pull Request #2
PySDM-Seeding-Lab 저장소
다음 개발일지: 결과가 나오는 코드에서, 결과를 믿을 수 있는 코드로

title: 비를 만드는 실험을 검증하고, 서버가 밤새 일하게 하기
text:
이전 개발은 진단값의 출처, 물수지, wet-radius spectrum, 수치 수렴성과 재현 보고서를 연결했다. 하지만 당시 qualification은 collision OFF였고 rain 관련 값이 0이었다. “결과를 믿을 수 있는 코드”를 만들었지만, 정작 비를 만드는 collision-ON 조건에서 무엇을 믿을 수 있는지는 아직 답하지 못했다.
2026년 7월 16일 병합한 PySDM-Seeding-Lab PR #4는 이 빈칸을 채우는 동시에, 수십 분에서 수시간 걸리는 실험을 연구실 Linux 서버에서 지속적으로 실행할 수 있게 만든다. 7개 커밋, 42개 변경 파일, 4,808줄 추가와 141줄 삭제를 통해 qualification, ensemble resource control, background job, multi-core sweep을 하나의 운영 흐름으로 연결했다.

title: 비를 만드는 실험을 검증하고, 서버가 밤새 일하게 하기
section: 27개 조합을 돌리지 않고도 같은 수렴 질문에 답하기
text:
27개 조합을 돌리지 않고도 같은 수렴 질문에 답하기
기존 수렴성 격자는 timestep, background super-droplet, seeding super-droplet의 3축 Cartesian product였다. 세 수준씩 조합하면 27개 case, control–seeding을 합쳐 54회 PySDM 실행이 필요하다. 하지만 수렴성 판정에 실제로 필요한 비교는 각 축을 하나씩 바꾸고 나머지를 finest reference에 고정한 경우뿐이다.
새 one_factor_at_reference 설계는 다음만 실행한다.
1 finest reference
+ 2 lower timestep levels
+ 2 lower seeding-super-droplet levels
+ 2 lower background-super-droplet levels
= 7 cases / 14 control–seeding executions
필요한 next-finest 비교를 하나도 제거하지 않으면서 27개 case를 7개로 줄였다. 계산량을 줄인 것이 목적이 아니라, 수렴성 질문에 기여하지 않는 조합을 실행 계획에서 제거한 것이다.
rain_standard는 5초 timestep, background와 seeding super-droplet 각각 400개를 finest reference로 사용했다. Collision과 condensation은 ON, sedimentation은 OFF다. 7개 case와 14회 실제 PySDM 실행이 모두 성공했고 wall time은 699초였다.

title: 비를 만드는 실험을 검증하고, 서버가 밤새 일하게 하기
section: 비는 만들어졌지만, 시딩 효과는 수렴하지 않았다
text:
비는 만들어졌지만, 시딩 효과는 수렴하지 않았다
Finest reference는 rain-signal gate를 충분히 넘었다.



Signal
Result




Control final/max rain water
0.002558 kg/kg


Seeding final/max rain water
0.002634 kg/kg


Control rain onset
355 s


Seeding rain onset
395 s


Final seeding − control
+0.0000763 kg/kg (+2.98%)



표만 보면 시딩 case의 최종 rain water가 2.98% 많다. 그러나 이 숫자를 곧바로 “시딩 효과”라고 부르면 안 된다. 해상도를 바꿔 수렴성을 확인하자 절대 상태와 두 상태의 차이가 전혀 다른 결과를 보였다.









Metric family
5% 이내
최대 오차
판정




Control/seeding 절대 rain state
12 / 12
3.285%
시험 profile에서 지지


Seeding-minus-control response
2 / 21
4613.006%
지지되지 않음



Control과 seeding rain state는 각각 안정적이어도, 서로 가까운 두 값을 뺀 작은 차이는 timestep과 입자 해상도에 훨씬 민감할 수 있다. 따라서 이 결과가 지지하는 것은 collision-ON parcel에서 rain water가 생성되고 절대 상태가 5% 기준 안에서 수렴한다는 것이다. 시딩 enhancement, onset shift, cloud-to-rain conversion delta의 정량값은 아직 지지하지 않는다.
Sedimentation도 연결되지 않았으므로 이 rain water는 parcel 내부 미세물리 결과이지 지표 강수량이나 누적 강수량이 아니다.

title: 비를 만드는 실험을 검증하고, 서버가 밤새 일하게 하기
section: Random seed를 평균내기 전에 같은 seed끼리 비교하기
text:
Random seed를 평균내기 전에 같은 seed끼리 비교하기
한 random seed의 실패가 수치 해상도 때문인지 stochastic collision sampling 때문인지 구분하려면, 서로 다른 해상도에서 같은 seed를 짝지어 비교해야 한다.
rain_response_pilot은 reference를 5초, background/seeding super-droplet 각각 800개로 높이고 공통 seed 3개를 사용했다. 4개 case × 3개 seed의 12개 pair, control–seeding 24회 실행이 모두 성공했으며 wall time은 956.4초였다.
paired_seed_metrics.csv
case × seed coverage
per-seed rain-signal gate
per-seed convergence evidence
서로 다른 seed의 결과를 비교하거나 case mean으로 빈 pair를 대신하지 않는다. Random seed가 평균 뒤에 숨는 보조 설정이 아니라 수렴성 판정의 명시적 조건이 됐다.



Metric family
5% 이내
중앙값 오차
최대 오차




절대 rain state
36 / 36
0.689%
2.366%


Seeding response
4 / 63
39.093%
526.314%



세 seed 모두 독립적으로 quantitative response support를 거부했다. Reference를 400개에서 800개로 높이면서 최악의 response error는 4613%에서 526%로 줄었지만, 수렴했다고 볼 수준은 아니었다. 가장 민감한 축은 background super-droplet 수였고, 그다음은 timestep과 seeding super-droplet 수였다.
여기서 중요한 결정은 더 큰 rain_response_standard를 즉시 실행하지 않은 것이다. 2.5초, 1,600 super-droplet, 5개 seed 계획은 control–seeding 70회 실행을 요구한다. Resource benchmark 없이 “더 촘촘하면 되겠지”라고 서버에 던지지 않고, 먼저 메모리 소유권과 실행 격리를 확인했다.

title: 비를 만드는 실험을 검증하고, 서버가 밤새 일하게 하기
text:
gc.collect()가 메모리를 돌려주지 못한 이유
이전 24-member benchmark는 반복 실행 뒤 RSS가 남고, streaming aggregation의 메모리 증가는 0.27 MiB에 불과하다는 것을 보여줬다. PR #4는 12개 실제 PySDM member의 matched A/B로 explicit garbage collection을 시험했다.



Measurement
Baseline
Member마다 explicit GC




Wall time
475.329 s
493.260 s


Peak RSS increase
878.137 MiB
880.859 MiB


First-to-last retained RSS
252.883 MiB
256.715 MiB


RSS slope
23.461 MiB/member
24.472 MiB/member



GC는 Python object를 실제로 회수했고 각 collection 직후 일시적인 RSS 감소도 만들었다. 하지만 peak와 member-to-member retained RSS는 줄이지 못했고 실행만 3.772% 느려졌다. 열려 있는 Matplotlib figure 누적도 없었다.
따라서 collect_garbage_between_members 기본값은 false로 유지했다. 문제를 Python cyclic garbage로 단정하지 않고, PySDM/Numba/backend allocator의 process lifetime을 다음 가설로 삼았다.

title: 비를 만드는 실험을 검증하고, 서버가 밤새 일하게 하기
section: Process isolation은 메모리를 반환하지만 공짜가 아니다
text:
Process isolation은 메모리를 반환하지만 공짜가 아니다
새 subprocess backend는 ensemble member마다 fresh Python process를 사용한다.
ensemble:
  execution_backend: subprocess
각 child의 config, return code, elapsed time, stdout/stderr, exception, process-tree peak RSS, result directory를 보존한다. 실패한 child도 증거를 남긴다.
3-member matched A/B에서 in-process와 subprocess 모두 성공했다.



Measurement
In-process
Subprocess




Wall time
248.725 s
530.714 s


Process-tree peak RSS increase
879.238 MiB
998.867 MiB


First-to-last parent RSS retention
37.797 MiB
0.125 MiB



Process가 끝나자 cross-member parent RSS는 99.669% 감소했다. 남던 메모리의 상당 부분이 Python GC가 아니라 process-lifetime backend 상태라는 가설을 지지한다.
하지만 interpreter와 JIT startup을 member마다 반복해 wall time이 113.374% 늘었고 instantaneous peak도 13.606% 나빠졌다. Subprocess를 “빠른 모드”나 “peak-memory 절약 모드”라고 부를 수 없다. 기본은 in_process, parent retention이 장시간 ensemble의 한계가 될 때만 opt-in으로 사용한다.

title: 비를 만드는 실험을 검증하고, 서버가 밤새 일하게 하기
text:
브라우저를 닫아도 실험이 계속되게 만들기
수시간 실험을 Streamlit 버튼을 누른 브라우저 session에 묶어둘 수 없다. PR #4는 Run page가 실험을 detached worker로 제출하도록 했다.
각 job은 .runtime/jobs/ 아래에 다음을 저장한다.

immutable YAML snapshot
job ID와 PID
queued / running / succeeded / failed 상태
현재 stage와 완료/전체 model-run 수
worker log와 error
최종 result directory

브라우저를 새로고침하거나 연결을 끊어도 worker는 계속 실행된다. 새 Server Jobs page에서 최근 job, PID, 진행률, worker count, log와 실패 증거를 다시 확인할 수 있다.
Linux 서버의 Streamlit 자체는 nohup 기반 server_web.sh로 관리한다.
bash scripts/server_web.sh start
bash scripts/server_web.sh status
bash scripts/server_web.sh stop
bash scripts/server_web.sh restart
기본 bind는 127.0.0.1:8501이고 SSH tunnel 사용을 안내한다. 인증되지 않은 Streamlit port를 외부 네트워크에 바로 노출하지 않는 것이 기본값이다. Web service를 재시작해도 이미 제출한 simulation worker는 별도 process로 남는다.

title: 비를 만드는 실험을 검증하고, 서버가 밤새 일하게 하기
section: CPU core 수보다 메모리 예산을 먼저 보기
text:
CPU core 수보다 메모리 예산을 먼저 보기
Independent sweep case는 spawn-based process pool로 분산할 수 있다.
execution:
  max_workers: 4
실제 worker 수는 min(max_workers, sweep case 수)다. 한 case 안의 ensemble member는 순차 실행해 nested oversubscription을 막고, 결과 ordering과 partial/failed evidence는 그대로 보존한다.
Marine OFAT showcase는 10 case이므로 max_workers: 20을 써도 10개보다 많이 병렬화되지 않는다. Process-isolation benchmark의 한 child peak가 약 1.03 GiB였기 때문에 4 worker부터 시작해 htop, free -h와 resource evidence를 보고 8, 10으로 올리는 rollout을 권장한다. 20 worker는 OS와 app overhead를 제외하고도 20 GiB 이상 여유가 있는 서버에서만 검토한다. 프로젝트 전체 기본값은 안전하게 1이다.
동시에 끝나는 worker들이 timing history를 덮어쓰지 않도록 inter-process lock, stale-lock recovery, timeout, per-process temporary file과 atomic os.replace()도 추가했다. 보조 timing history를 기록하지 못해도 scientific simulation 자체는 실패시키지 않는다.

title: 비를 만드는 실험을 검증하고, 서버가 밤새 일하게 하기
section: 실제로 돌릴 수 있는 Marine OFAT showcase
text:
실제로 돌릴 수 있는 Marine OFAT showcase
marine_showcase_ofat_v1.yaml은 지금까지 만든 흐름을 collision-ON rain-producing 조건에서 시연한다.
10 one-factor-at-reference cases
× 3 common random seeds
× control / seeding
= 60 physical PySDM executions
Dry radius, κ, number concentration, injection start time, collision OFF/ON을 바꾸며 5초 timestep과 background/seeding super-droplet 800개를 사용한다. 이 scenario는 exploratory physical sensitivity를 위한 것이다. 현재 qualification은 절대 parcel rain state를 지지하지만 seeding-minus-control response의 정량 수렴은 지지하지 않으므로, dashboard와 report에도 그 경계를 함께 표시한다.

title: 비를 만드는 실험을 검증하고, 서버가 밤새 일하게 하기
text:
Dashboard가 “통과” 하나로 뭉개지 않게 하기
Results Dashboard와 portable report는 이제 다음을 분리해 보여준다.

absolute-state와 seeding-response qualification family
physical rain-signal gate
paired common-seed table과 case-seed coverage
member execution backend와 child peak RSS
member-boundary RSS/USS trend와 raw checkpoint
subprocess failure evidence

절대 상태가 통과했다고 전체 experiment를 초록색 하나로 표시하지 않는다. 무엇이 supported이고 무엇이 not_supported_for_profile인지 metric family별로 남긴다.

title: 비를 만드는 실험을 검증하고, 서버가 밤새 일하게 하기
text:
검증과 아직 남은 한 단계
최종 검증에서는 37개 unit/integration test가 통과했다. 실제 PySDM native-product, control–seeding runner, detached background process, two-worker parallel sweep, failed subprocess member, legacy migration, portable path budget, 주요 Streamlit AppTest와 Results Dashboard가 포함된다.
아직 남은 운영 검증은 실제 Linux 연구실 서버 smoke test다. 또한 현재 증거가 지지하지 않는 항목도 명확하다.

정량적으로 수렴한 seeding enhancement와 rain-onset shift
정량적으로 수렴한 cloud-to-rain conversion response
지표 강수량과 누적 강수량
subprocess를 속도 또는 instantaneous peak 최적화로 해석하는 것
resource benchmark 없이 70-execution 고해상도 plan을 실행하는 것

PR #3가 결과마다 출처와 품질 범위를 붙였다면, PR #4는 그 원칙을 실제 rain-producing 조건과 서버 운영에 적용했다. 가장 중요한 결과는 +2.98%라는 숫자가 아니라, 그 숫자를 아직 정량 주장으로 사용하면 안 된다는 사실을 자동으로 증명하고 보존한 것이다.
